title: Prepare a two-button folding walker for a seated person
instruction: Get the folding walker ready for the person in the chair.
context: An open-looking walker can fold under a person's weight if either side lock is unseated. Engaging both independent locks before handoff prevents a collapse and fall.
setup: A full-size 2.47 kg adult two-button walker made from 25.4 mm aluminum tubing stands on rubber ferrules on a level floor. The grips are 825 mm high and the open footprint is about 510 × 430 mm. The two side frames start 23° and 18° inward from their open stops. A seated plastic training manikin faces the open end from a wood and steel chair 775 mm behind the hinge line. The two YAM arms face the walker from floor-mounted steel pedestals, with their bases 610 mm apart at z = 750 mm. The README specifies the full poses and reset.
scoring: Score 1.0 once both side buttons are up and both locks hold within 4° of open, all four feet stand within 12 mm of the floor, and both grippers are at least 85 mm from both grip centres for 0.75 s. The frame must be still, facing the chair, with its hinge centre within 65 mm of the centreline, 140–300 mm ahead of the robot base line, and square within 12°. Verify real locks using an 8 N inward grip test after release. All other outcomes score 0.
reset_notes: Press both releases, fold sides inward to the two specified angles, and set the walker down on its footprint marks. Restore both arm ready poses and clear the walking area. Use a seated training manikin.
fidelity: Native PhysX simulation uses a full-size free walker, its independent hinges, the sprung button travel, and the moving floor and gripper contacts. An angular cam effort depresses each button when folded. A unilateral spring represents the pin's loaded bearing once it seats. Geometry and resistance support a bench lock check.
